chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel, and Ibn Bukayr, and Hammad ibn Usman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The perpetrator of Zahaar, when he divorces, the expiation drops off from him.
ai.seo_question: Does divorce cancel the Zahaar expiation in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the ritual expiation (kaffarah) for Zahaar is contingent upon the marriage bond remaining intact; thus, if the husband divorces his wife, the obligation is lifted. This ruling highlights the juristic view that Zahaar is a specific impediment to marital intimacy rather than a permanent sin, distinguishing it from other forms of expiation. It reflects the practical legal reasoning found in Shia fiqh where the remedy is tied to the restoration of the marital state.
